subject: Zipline: tenor restructure + phased commit proposal
messages:
From: Suhani Patel <suhani@openminds.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T14:05:00Z
Subject: Renewal window — exploring multi-year structure with phased commitments

Hi Aditya,

Quick note as we start our renewal planning: our leadership wants to move to a multi-year agreement but keep flexibility for quarterly increases tied to usage — they called it a "phased commit" approach.

High level ask: can Redwood put together a proposal that smooths the year 1 to year 2 ramp (we expect ~2.5x growth), includes an auto-renew opt-in with a 60-day notice-out, and a clear path for adding burst capacity during product launches? We tried to sketch an internal model and attached a simple table.

Questions for you:
- Is co-terming across our three subsidiaries possible under one contract?
- Any recommended guardrails for price protections if we significantly outgrow the committed band?

Attaching the usage table for reference (summary). Ben Lewis is on copy for procurement.

Thanks,
Suhani
Suhani Patel
Head of Platform Strategy, Nimbus Analytics
attachments: zipline_commit_table.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Suhani Patel <suhani@openminds.ai>
Cc: Ben Lewis <ben@cloudops.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window — exploring multi-year structure with phased commitments

Hi Suhani — thanks for the clear brief and the table, this is helpful. I pulled a quick sketch together and attached a proposal (Nimbus_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf) with a recommended model that aims to balance price predictability and flexibility:

Proposal highlights (quick):
- 3-year commitment with year-over-year stepped commit (15% ramp Y1, 60% Y2, 25% Y3) tied to quarterly checkpoints
- Quarterly true-up window (30 days after quarter) to handle overages with a blended rate cap
- Auto-renew opt-in with 60-day notice-out and a fixed CPI-style floor for price changes
- Co-terming: yes — we can consolidate subsidiaries on a single master agreement with per-entity usage buckets and a master SLA
- Burst policy: pre-agreed burst pool (up to 1.5x baseline) billable at discounted overage rate; option to purchase temporary burst credits in advance

Next steps: if this direction looks right, I can loop in Contracts for redlines and Camila for PS/onboarding cadence. Do you want us to include an early-upsize credit if you frontload usage in Q1?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Nimbus_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window — exploring multi-year structure with phased commitments

Aditya — saw this, good baseline. Quick thoughts from GTM/PS:

- Early-upsize credit: we can offer a single-use frontload credit equal to 15% of Y1 committed spend if they purchase within 30 days of signing. That helps them accelerate onboarding while protecting revenue.
- Burst discount: 20% off list for pre-purchased burst credits is reasonable, but let's limit to 3x baseline for safety (instead of 1.5x) or staggered tiers (1.25x at 25% discount, 2x at 15%, 3x at 10%). I prefer the tiered approach — gives them flexibility and limits our tail risk.
- Implementation cadence: if they elect the phased commit we should include a milestone-driven ramp plan tied to admin onboarding and model migration checkpoints (quarterly). I'll include a PS estimate in the draft SOW.

Marissa — on the legal side we should be able to support a master agreement with per-entity exhibit. 60-day auto-renew notice is fine but recommend adding a 3% maximum annual pricing adjustment cap outside of CPI to give legal a guardrail.

If you both agree, I'll draft the SOW language and forward to Contracts for redlines.

Camila
Camila Reyes
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Suhani Patel <suhani@openminds.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Lewis <ben@cloudops.com>, Contracts <contracts@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Zipline tenor restructure + phased commit proposal

Thanks all — this looks like the right framework. A few confirmation points from our side before we move to signature:

- We accept the 3-year stepped commit with the tiered burst credit option (we'll start at the 1.25x tier and reserve the right to move up).
- Please include the 15% frontload credit for Y1 as part of the commercial summary.
- Co-terming via master agreement + per-entity exhibits is acceptable. Our Contracts team will review legal language; Contracts (on copy) will route to our procurement POC.

Can you send the updated proposal and a DocuSign packet with standard SOW and master agreement? We aim to have this signed before Oct 15 to align budget cycles.

Appreciate the quick turn.
Suhani
